title: Cap. IX Arg.: Adam's sin remitted to all — God cannot leave anyone in that condemnation by strict right alone
pass_a_gloss: From the sin of Adam remitted unto all promiscuously they so dispute: God is not able to deal by strict right with any man lying in the common sin of Adam, so that he be left in that condemnation without any hope of pardon: But if he were to reprobate any only as lying in the common fall of Adam, and not on account of their actual and personal rebellion against God, he would deal with them by strict and highest right.
pass_b_english: From Adam's sin remitted to all alike they argue thus: God cannot deal by strict right with any man lying in Adam's common sin so as to leave him in that condemnation without any hope of pardon. But if he reprobated any only as lying in Adam's common fall, and not for their actual personal rebellion against God, he would be dealing with them by strict and highest right.
source_text: Ab Adae peccato omnibus promiscue remisso sic disputant: Deus non valet stricto jure agere cum ullo homine in communi Adae peccato jacente, ita ut sine ulla spe veniae in ista condemnatione relinquatur: At si reprobaret quospiam tantum ut jacentes in lapsu communi Adae, et non propter actualem eorum et personalem in Deum rebellionem, stricto et summo jure cum illis ageret.
notes: Densify De praedestinatione Cap. IX Ab Adae section 579. Pass A!=B. Packet praedestinatione_cap9_ab_adae_densify. Accurate over pretty.
